title: Joseph Frederick Commutation Remains Unverified
description_short: The DOJ commutations list does not identify Joseph Frederick; a case-specific clemency warrant is missing.
description_medium: The linked Justice Department page lists commutations granted by President Trump from 2017 through 2021, but a focused search found no “Joseph Frederick” entry. The packet supplies no offense, sentence, commutation date, or warrant that could confirm the person’s identity and clemency action. Keep the record on hold unless a primary warrant or reliable case-specific record is found; absence from this page alone does not prove that no such action occurred.
description_long: The frozen record asserts that President Trump commuted Joseph Frederick’s sentence on December 24, 2018, but provides no warrant, case number, offense, sentence, or terms. The official DOJ index covers Trump’s 2017–2021 commutations; the previous audit reports that a focused search of that index found no “Joseph Frederick,” “Joseph,” or “Frederick” entry. That absence is limited to the linked index and does not prove that no separate clemency instrument exists. For this final attempt, one focused Exa search asked for an official warrant or docket linking Joseph Frederick to the claimed date and commutation. Exa returned HTTP 504 before providing results, so there is no new source to assess. The recipient-to-warrant linkage and the alleged action remain unverified. Keep the record on hold pending an identifiable primary instrument or case-specific reliable record; do not state the commutation occurred and do not infer that it did not.

supported_facts: The page heading reads “Commutations granted by President Donald J. Trump (2017–2021).”
The supplied prior source audit reports no match for “Joseph Frederick,” “Joseph,” or “Frederick” in a focused search of this index.
limitations: The index’s missing-name result does not establish that no separate clemency warrant exists or that no commutation occurred.

final_attempt.result: Transport failure: HTTP 504; no search results or source URLs returned. No new source was read.

The one permitted new focused search failed with HTTP 504 and returned no source to evaluate. The prior DOJ index no-match cannot establish that no separate clemency action occurred.
rationale: Maintain the prior hold. The new focused Exa query for an official warrant or docket returned HTTP 504 with no sources, and no genuinely new evidence supports either the claimed commutation or a narrower same-event correction. Preserve the prior DOJ-index limitation and do not turn an unverified event into an exclusion claim.
